claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 healthy controls showed a significant reduction in the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) and decreased mTOR signaling in pDCs of infected individuals.

sources.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts.

We used mass cytometry to assess immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in 52 COVID-19 patients, who were confirmed positive for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls distributed between the two cohorts.

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of ex vivo stimulated PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls.

claim_3.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed significant upregulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection.

claim_4.claim: Q-PCR analysis of plasma from severe and ICU COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA and LPS compared to healthy individuals.

sources.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product, and of LPS, as measured by a TLR4-based reporter assay.

claim_5.claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing (CITE-seq) analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients revealed clusters of T cells and monocytes characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15.

sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15.
